output.classification_reasoning: The incident is driven by a BGP flap on a transit gateway, which is a clear network-layer event. The flap caused a temporary loss of routing stability, leading to a secondary telemetry spike in the search-indexer service and a brief 17‑minute outage for a limited user set (25 users). While the root cause is confined to network routing, diagnosing BGP flaps typically requires analysis of routing tables, gateway health, and potential upstream provider interactions, adding more steps than a simple connectivity loss. However, the impact is bounded to a single service and a short duration, indicating the overall effort is not highly intricate. Therefore, the failure is classified as a network_failure with moderate operational complexity.

output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

output.governing_sla_rule: Minor disruption impacting < 100 users with standard SLA.
output.justification: The incident affects 25 users, well below the 100‑user threshold for a minor disruption. The outage duration is 17 minutes, which is within the acceptable window for Tier‑3 services under the standard SLA. The diagnostic stage is "Root Cause Confirmed" with a high confidence score (0.95), confirming the issue is isolated to a known network failure pattern in the search-indexer service. According to corporate severity thresholds, these parameters map to SEV-4.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Operator Access and Kubernetes Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the executing engineer has the required ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us‑east‑1.
verification: AWS identity ARN includes ProdOperations role

remediation_steps.title: Enforce Write‑Freeze on Search‑Indexer Primary
remediation_steps.description: Prevent new write traffic to the primary indexer node while remediation actions are performed.
verification: kubectl rollout status shows deployment is paused

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica to Primary
remediation_steps.description: Elevate the healthy read‑replica to serve write traffic, ensuring continuity before any node reboot.

remediation_steps.title: Reboot Affected Worker Node(s) to Reset BGP Session
remediation_steps.description: Perform a controlled node reboot to clear the BGP flap on the transit gateway. Follow the runbook's write‑freeze note before reboot.
verification: Node status returns Ready after reboot
BGP session shows Established (via network monitoring tool)
No new ERR_NETWORK_FAILURE_400 logs for 5 minutes

remediation_steps.title: Resume Deployment and Remove Write‑Freeze
remediation_steps.description: Bring the search‑indexer deployment back to normal operation and lift the write‑freeze.

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Confirm that the service is fully functional and that error rates have returned to baseline.
commands: kubectl logs deployment/search-indexer --tail=100 | grep ERR_NETWORK_FAILURE_400 || true
verification: No ERR_NETWORK_FAILURE_400 entries in recent logs

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert promotion of the read‑replica, restore the original primary node configuration, and undo the write‑freeze removal. All actions are idempotent and can be executed in reverse order of the remediation steps.

steps.description: Demote the promoted replica back to read‑only and re‑assign original primary role.
verification: Primary role label is removed from former primary

steps.description: Re‑apply write‑freeze to prevent accidental writes during rollback.
Rollback any container image changes made during remediation (if applicable).
verification: Deployment revision is set to previous stable version

steps.description: If node reboot caused issues, power the node back on to the pre‑reboot snapshot.
verification: Node re‑joins the cluster as Ready

steps.description: Remove write‑freeze after confirming service stability.
